landmarks.what: lanes may declare a free-form selector template and join; validate refuses one with no selector, no placeholder, or a join with no {paths}

{path} repeats the template per path and {paths} substitutes them into one instance (joined when declared); the sole shell quoter moves here so template text and substituted path are quoted by one implementation

a third length-framed consent namespace binds selector_template and selector_join beside command and prepare, so declaring or changing either stales the grant while an untemplated lane keeps its pre-phase fingerprint

a lane declaring a selector_template places its derived paths through testlane.Expand instead of appending them; the up-front fence expands against no paths so a malformed template refuses before any lane spawns and the header prints the exact expanded line

lane edit now rewrites match, command, selector, empty_exit, selector_template and selector_join in place keeping the grant (only the name is still remove-then-re-add); both verbs gate on the whole lane's laneProblems over a synthetic one-lane project

validate gains a warning tier that never changes exit status; a lane scoping onto a command ending in ./... or . is warned about by name at declaration time and on every validate run, and still written

README and options.md gain the selector template surface, the widened lane edit field set and the whole-tree warning; the remove-then-re-add guard is re-pointed to the lane name and the flag-name guard widened to lane edit
the sole CLI gate for a proposed lane, after the orphaned per-field-group laneSelectorRefusal it had already subsumed was deleted
